steps.text:
**Risk factors that Mayo Clinic lists for all three types of aneurysm (abdominal‑aortic, brain, and thoracic‑aortic)** | Common risk factor | How it shows up in each Mayo Clinic page | |--------------------|------------------------------------------| | **Older age** | *Abdominal aortic aneurysm* – “Smoking is the strongest risk factor…” and the page notes that it is more common in men over 65【1†source】.
*Brain aneurysm* – “Risk factors include: Age. Brain aneurysms can happen at any age.”【3†source】.
*Thoracic aortic aneurysm* – “Thoracic aortic aneurysm risk factors include: Age. Thoracic aortic aneurysms occur most often in people age 65 and older.”【5†source】 | | **Cigarette smoking** | *Abdominal aortic aneurysm* – “Smoking is the strongest risk factor for aortic aneurysms.”【1†source】.
*Brain aneurysm* – “Cigarette smoking.”【3†source】.
*Thoracic aortic aneurysm* – “Smoking and tobacco use.”【5†source】 | | **High blood pressure (hypertension)** | *Abdominal aortic aneurysm* – “…increased high blood pressure…”.【1†source】.
*Brain aneurysm* – “High blood …” under risk factors【3†source】.
*Thoracic aortic aneurysm* – “High blood pressure, also called hypertension.”【5†source】 | | **Family history of aneurysm** | *Abdominal aortic aneurysm* – “…a family history of abdominal aortic aneurysms.”【1†source】.
*Brain aneurysm* – “If you have a family history….”【3†source】.
*Thoracic aortic aneurysm* – “…family history of aortic aneurysm.”【5†source】 | **Bottom line** Across the three Mayo Clinic disease pages, the *over‑all common risk factors* are **older age, cigarette smoking, hypertension (high blood pressure), and a family history of aneurysm**. These four risk factors are listed for each of the three aneurysm types, making them the shared set of contributors to the development of an abdominal aortic aneurysm, a brain aneurysm, and a thoracic aortic aneurysm.
